problems.field: studies[S3].outcomes[S3-O3].contrasts[0].control_arm and comparison_type (and the outcome's question and ai_available_when_produced, which rest on the same arm pairing)
problems.form_value: treatment_arm 'ChatGPT (the main text does not say whether this means the ChatGPT-assisted ideas, the ChatGPT-only responses or both)'; control_arm 'Human-only (comparison group not named in the main text)'; comparison_type 'ai_vs_bau'; question 'with_ai'; ai_available_when_produced 'yes'
problems.source_says: The main text names no comparison group for the newness-type result. It also does not say whether 'ChatGPT' means the randomized ChatGPT-assisted participants or the 100 ChatGPT-only responses that no participant produced. The hypothesis was tested by classifying 'each response' (PDF p. 3), which includes the ChatGPT-only responses, and the numbers are only in Supplementary Note G, which is not in this PDF. A randomized AI-versus-no-AI contrast (ai_vs_bau, with_ai, AI available) is therefore not supported. If the ChatGPT-only responses are in the 'ChatGPT' group, the comparison is AI output versus human output (ai_vs_human, question none, ai_available_when_produced mixed).
problems.quote: Analysis of expert judges’ ratings revealed that ChatGPT is particularly effective at generating incrementally new ideas but less effective at generating radically new ideas (see Supplementary Note G for the details).
problems.locator: PDF p. 3 (journal p. 1908), Results, Experiment 2B; the hypothesis sentence 'We tested this hypothesis by classifying the type of creativity featured in each response' is on the same page

problems.form_value: Participants interacted with ChatGPT until they found a satisfactory response, then modified it as needed, and reported how much they relied on it.
problems.source_says: Minor. The paper reports an instruction, not observed behavior: participants were asked to interact with ChatGPT until satisfied and then modify as needed. The reliance self-report is stated as fact in the paper and is correct. Suggested wording: 'Participants were asked to interact with ChatGPT until they found a satisfactory response and then modify it as needed; they reported how much they relied on it.'
problems.quote: Specifically, they were asked to interact with ChatGPT until they found a satisfactory response and then make more modifications as needed on the basis of the response from ChatGPT.

problems.form_value: S5: 'Participants assigned to the ChatGPT condition used ChatGPT to come up with one creative gift idea.' S6: 'Participants in the ChatGPT-assisted condition used ChatGPT to come up with one idea.'
problems.source_says: Minor. For Experiments 4 and 5 the text reports only assignment to the ChatGPT-assisted ('website') condition, and the abstract says participants were asked to use ChatGPT. No use or compliance measure is printed for these two experiments, so 'used ChatGPT' is not stated. Suggested wording: 'Participants assigned to the ChatGPT-assisted condition were asked to use ChatGPT to come up with one idea.'
problems.quote: Prolific participants were assigned to one of the two website conditions and were asked to come up with one creative gift idea for a teenage girl.
problems.locator: PDF p. 4 (journal p. 1909), Results, Experiment 4; Experiment 5 at PDF pp. 4-5 (journal pp. 1909-1910), Results; abstract, PDF p. 1

summary: The PDF states random, between-participants assignment of individual MTurk or Prolific participants to ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) versus traditional Web search and/or a no-aid Human-only condition in all six experiments, and the form's assignment fields, arms and quotes for S1-S6 match it (Methods, PDF pp. 6-8; Reporting Summary, PDF p. 11). The coding is still refuted in parts: the Experiment 2B newness-type contrast (S3-O3) codes a Human-only control and ai_vs_bau that the main text does not state, because its 'ChatGPT' group may be the non-randomized ChatGPT-only responses, and the how_used text for S3, S5 and S6 reports ChatGPT use where the paper reports only instructions or assignment.
